tier_reason: The README states 'About 30% faster' than the hardware div instruction 'At least on Intel', but the repo holds only LICENSE, README.md and fast-divide.h: no benchmark code, no timing table, no CPU model and no compiler version. A first-party percentage without methodology is tier C (borderline D).

corrections.caveats: Only a prose claim ('About 30% faster', 'At least on Intel, where div is crazy slow'); the repo has no benchmark source, numbers, CPU model or compiler version, so results on cores with a faster 64-bit divider (newer Intel and AMD) may differ. The README itself warns that the routine uses more registers than a single div and that spilling can erase the gain, and that compile-time-constant divisors should be left to the compiler. Division or modulo by 0 is undefined (no trap). The only timing the author posted (issue #1) compares the library's C and inline-asm versions (0.310 vs 0.283, units and CPU unstated), not the hardware div. A divider-class bug was fixed on 2021-02-17 (commit 'fix issue in divider class (standalone funcs unaffected)'); the last commit is a README edit on 2021-09-30.

notes: Real, MIT, 32 stars, 24 commits, abandoned since 2021-09-30; claim is a single unmeasured percentage with no harness, so it stays at C (could be argued D). Scalar integer division, not SIMD: libdivide and fastmod are filed under math-simd-linear-algebra, so the orchestrator may want a category override to sit next to them; no independent benchmark of this repo was found by search.

tier_reason: The README says Div, Mod and DivMod for U128 on Haswell+ are 'about 2x faster than the compiler-rt stuff' (__udivti3, __umodti3, __udivmodti4); the repo has only fast-div-128.h/.cpp, README and LICENSE, with no benchmark code, numbers table, CPU model or compiler version. First-party figure without methodology: tier C (borderline D).

corrections.caveats: Prose claim only ('about 2x faster than the compiler-rt stuff'): no benchmark source, numbers, CPU model or compiler version. The baseline is compiler-rt's generic routine (which the README notes is also missing on Clang for Windows), not libgcc's __udivti3, a tuned library such as GMP, or a hand-written div-based 128/64 path. The library targets Clang with inline assembly; the README says GCC builds but with worse codegen, and x86 Haswell or newer is required. The whole history is six commits on 2021-02-14.

notes: Real, MIT, 4 stars, 6 commits all on 2021-02-14, abandoned; '2x' is an unmeasured README figure, kept at C as the record had it (could be argued D). Same author and category question as FastDivide: libdivide sits in math-simd-linear-algebra.

tier_reason: README 'Experimental results' table (GCC, 'a Skylake processor') matches the record exactly, and the harness is public (benchmarks/benchmark.c, rdtsc best-of-5 via benchmarks/benchmark.h) with Makefile flags -std=c99 -march=native -O3; the CPU model and GCC version are missing, so not A. The Keiser and Lemire SPE 2021 paper the README cites covers the later lookup algorithm (simdjson/simdutf), not this repo's 2018 code, so it does not lift the tier.

corrections.caveats: README marks the library obsolete as of 2022 and says it is for demonstration, not production; simdutf (already catalogued) carries the newer lookup algorithm. Benchmark CPU is named only as Skylake and the GCC version is missing, so tier C. Cycles are rdtsc reference cycles, best of 5 runs on 64 KiB buffers. The only baseline in the README table is a byte-at-a-time Guava-derived scalar validator with an ASCII fast path; the current benchmark.c also times Hoehrmann-style DFA validators (added after issue #24, 2020) whose results are not in the README, so the published table predates the current harness. The ASCII rows favour schemes that skip ASCII quickly (the program prints this); validate_ascii_fast and validate_ascii_fast_avx are ASCII-only checks, not UTF-8 validators. Harness fixes after the README numbers: issue #25 (elapsed seconds mis-scaled, closed 2024-03-13; affects only the time output, not the cycle counts) and issue #27 (populate wrote one byte past the buffer; the current populate no longer does). The two cited lemire.me blog posts (2018) could not be opened. x64 SSE/AVX only, no ARM.

notes: Numbers and derived ratios check out (10.967/0.702 = 15.6x, 10.967/0.448 = 24.5x, 1.256/0.704 = 1.8x, 1.256/0.450 = 2.8x). Not a duplicate: it is the 2018 predecessor of simdutf and the baseline of the catalogued protobuf utf8_range entry; it fits wave 3's unicode-utf8 category better than simd-intrinsics-libraries (category plus domain override if moved). 309 stars, last commit 2024-03-13 (stale), Apache-2.0 OR BSL-1.0 OR MIT (repo root has LICENSE-APACHE, LICENSE-BOOST and LICENSE-MIT).
